1|# Contracts
2|
3|Music generation must never block the reader. Each module below owns one
4|job and can be swapped without touching the others. Import direction is
5|`core <- server` and `core <- app`. Server and client components never
6|import each other. `app/page.tsx` may import `server/books.ts`. Client
7|files never do.
8|
9|## Book data
10|
11|`data/books/oz/book.json` holds the frozen text: id, title, author,
12|`textVersion` hash, chapters with `start_n` and `end_n`, and paragraphs
13|with `id`, `ch`, `n`, and `text`. `analysis.json` is the scene source
14|the reader consumes: the same scenes plus Jev vectors, the Muse
15|override, and the `final` emotion. `scenes.json` is the pipeline
16|intermediate that `analysis.json` mirrors. The reader consumes the book
17|fields, scene ranges and titles, and the `final` vector with intensity
18|and tempo. It never sees `jev`, `muse_override`, or provenance.
19|`core/reader.ts` defines `buildReaderModel`, which joins paragraphs to
20|scenes by ordinal range and throws on unordered scenes or on paragraphs
21|covered zero or two times.
22|
23|## Music library
24|
25|The library is a static `public/music/manifest.json`, version 2, fetched
26|by the client from `/music/manifest.json`. A static file needs no route,
27|ships from the CDN, and swaps by replacing files only. Tracks may be
28|several minutes long and are not loops unless marked so.
29|
30|`MusicManifest = { version, tracks }`. `Track = { id, src, title,
31|emotion, vector, intensity, tempo, durationSec }` plus optional
32|`startSec` (default 0, where playback starts on first play and on each
33|loop), `loop` (default true), `source` (`generated`, `jamendo`, or
34|`recording`), `artist`, `composer`, `license`, `attribution`, and
35|`sourceUrl` (https only). `emotion` is the hand label: one of the 8
36|emotion ids in `core/types.ts`. The vector covers the 8 ids with finite
37|entries in 0..1. `core/music.ts` owns `parseManifest`, which rejects
38|unknown versions, missing fields, bad vectors, NaN entries, out-of-range
39|numbers, `startSec` outside its range, unknown `source` values, and any
40|`src` that is not a `/music/` path or `https` URL. The reader calls it on
41|every fetch, so a bad drop-in fails loudly in dev. Remote URLs need a
42|`media-src` addition in `next.config.ts`.
43|
44|## Similarity and config
45|
46|`Similarity = (scene, track, weights) => number`, where
47|`SceneSignal = { vector, intensity, tempo }`. The default is
48|`bhattacharyyaSimilarity`: both 8-emotion vectors renormalize to sum 1
49|(an all-zero vector gives an affinity of 0), `E` is the sum of
50|`sqrt(s_k * t_k)`, and the score is `weights.emotion * E` plus
51|`weights.intensity` and `weights.tempo` each for intensity and tempo
52|closeness. Scoring and ranking pass the resolved config weights in, so
53|a weights override changes the ranking. `cosineSimilarity` over
54|`buildFeatures` output stays as an exported alternative. One exported object,
55|`MUSIC_CONFIG`, holds `similarity`, `weights`, `switchMargin` (0.07),
56|`dwellSec` (20), `minTrackSec` (45), `hardCutMargin` (0.20),
57|`crossfadeSec` (3), and `hardCutCrossfadeSec` (1.5). Everything else
58|reads from it. Ranking ties go to the lower track id.
59|
60|## Selection scheduler
61|
62|`core/music-schedule.ts` is a pure state machine. The reader calls
63|`observeScene`, `tickScheduler`, `requestNext`, and `noteTrackEnded`
64|with explicit `nowSec` values, so all timing is testable without
65|timers. State holds the current track id and when it started, the active
66|scene id, the pending scene id and since when, and the skip override
67|with the scene it belongs to.
68|
69|A newly entered scene becomes pending and the dwell clock restarts, so
70|fast scrolling keeps only the newest scene. The first track ever plays
71|at once with no dwell. After the pending scene holds for `dwellSec` it
72|becomes active and the override clears. Then the best track switches in
73|only when it beats the current score by `switchMargin` and the current
74|track played `minTrackSec`, unless it wins by `hardCutMargin` (hard
75|cut, short fade). A second passes the active scene back through the
76|switch check, so a hold from `minTrackSec` releases on time, unless a
77|skip override stands: ticks return no change while it is set, and only
78|a new scene promotion clears it. A switch
79|reports its crossfade length: 3 s normally,
80|1.5 s for hard cuts. The skip choice holds until the next scene change;
81|after that, dwell and hysteresis apply with the override track as the
82|current track. A null scene means a failed analysis with no vector, so
83|it never triggers a switch. A non-looping track that ends fades into
84|the best remaining track, excluding the one that ended, and clears the
85|skip override.
86|
87|## Change track
88|
89|`nextTrack` cycles tracks hand-labeled with the scene dominant emotion
90|(argmax of the renormalized scene vector, ties by emotion order), ranked
91|by score with ties by lower id, wrapping around and skipping the current
92|track. When the current track has another emotion, it starts at the top
93|candidate. With no other same-emotion track it falls back to the best
94|track overall that is not current. A null scene cycles all tracks in id
95|order. One track or none gives null, and the UI disables the button.
96|
97|## Player
98|
99|`app/player.tsx` takes the track, the fade length for the latest switch,
100|the scene title, a skip flag, and callbacks. It owns two `audio`
101|elements, play state, volume, and the equal-power crossfade
102|(cos/sin gains over the fade time, driven by `requestAnimationFrame`).
103|It never uses the `loop` attribute. Volume lives in a ref, so the slider
104|never re-runs the track effect or touches `src`. A new track request
105|mid-fade cancels the pending fade and fades from the audible element to
106|the newest track. On load each track seeks to `startSec` once metadata
107|is available. Long tracks with `loop` true crossfade into the other
108|element playing the same track from `startSec` when `currentTime`
109|reaches `duration - fade`, where `fade` is the latest scheduler fade
110|length, or the config `crossfadeSec` when none was reported yet. When
111|`loop` is false the player reports the end and the scheduler picks the
112|next-best track excluding the ended one. Pause stops both elements and
113|freezes the fade in place; play resumes the audible elements from the
114|frozen point. Audio starts once, on the first press, with fade 0.
115|Audio starts only after the user presses play. Reduced motion is read in
116|state with a change listener and affects visuals only, never the fade.
117|
118|The bar shows Play/Pause, Volume, a Change track button (disabled when
119|Next has nothing to offer), the track title with its emotion label, and
120|attribution when present: composer or artist, license, and a source
121|link. On manifest failure the reader still renders and the bar shows a
122|short neutral note. UI motion stays under 200 ms. Controls are real
123|buttons and inputs with labels, visible focus, and keyboard use.
124|
125|## Image api
126|
127|`POST /api/images` (Node runtime, `maxDuration` 120). Request is a
128|discriminated union: `{ kind: "passage", bookId, textVersion, n }` names
129|the paragraph where the selection starts, `{ kind: "scene", bookId,
130|textVersion, sceneId }` names the scene. Validation is strict: known
131|book, matching `textVersion`, integer `n` inside the book, known
132|`sceneId`. Any other body is a 400 with a generic Spanish message.
133|The client sends ordinals and ids only, never text.
134|
135|Responses (typed in `core/types.ts`): `{ status: "ready", url, cached,
136|caption }` with a Vercel Blob URL, never bytes; `{ status: "pending" }`
137|when another request holds the lock, in which case the client reposts
138|every 3 s up to about 2 minutes; `{ status: "error", code, message }`
139|where code is `quota`, `budget`, `unavailable`, or `bad_request` with a
140|friendly Spanish message. Caption is the scene title for scenes and the
141|first words of the paragraph for passages, built server-side.
142|
143|The passage cache key is book plus start paragraph plus `textVersion`
144|plus `PROMPT_VERSION` (`v1`); the scene key is book plus scene id plus
145|the same versions. Both map to a deterministic Blob path
146|(`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). An Upstash Redis
147|index maps key to Blob URL, so hits are one GET; on an index miss the
148|server checks the Blob path before generating and backfills the index.
149|A Redis lock per key returns `pending` to concurrent requests. Quota is
150|5 new images per person per day by hashed IP and signed cookie,
151|whichever runs out first; a shared spend counter in integer
152|micro-dollars sits under `SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 10). Failures refund
153|quota and budget and release the lock.
154|
155|## Chat api
156|
157|Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN,
158|spoilerMode, messages }` carries the chat history and the reader
159|position. The response is streamed text. The server builds context from
160|the book text up to `positionN`, or the whole book when `spoilerMode` is
161|on, with the book prefix first and the question last so readers share
162|the prompt cache. The system prompt answers only from that text and
163|refuses the rest. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
164|
165|## Quotas and budget
166|
167|Server only. Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars: reserve with
168|Redis `INCRBY` before each model call, refund with `DECRBY` after, one
169|reserve per call including retries. The server clamps every model tool
170|argument. Clients never see keys or raw errors. Generic messages go to
171|the client, details stay in server logs.

1|# Contracts
2|
3|Music generation must never block the reader. Each module below owns one
4|job and can be swapped without touching the others. Import direction is
5|`core <- server` and `core <- app`. Server and client components never
6|import each other. `app/page.tsx` may import `server/books.ts`. Client
7|files never do.
8|
9|## Book data
10|
11|`data/books/oz/book.json` holds the frozen text: id, title, author,
12|`textVersion` hash, chapters with `start_n` and `end_n`, and paragraphs
13|with `id`, `ch`, `n`, and `text`. `analysis.json` is the scene source
14|the reader consumes: the same scenes plus Jev vectors, the Muse
15|override, and the `final` emotion. `scenes.json` is the pipeline
16|intermediate that `analysis.json` mirrors. The reader consumes the book
17|fields, scene ranges and titles, and the `final` vector with intensity
18|and tempo. It never sees `jev`, `muse_override`, or provenance.
19|`core/reader.ts` defines `buildReaderModel`, which joins paragraphs to
20|scenes by ordinal range and throws on unordered scenes or on paragraphs
21|covered zero or two times.
22|
23|## Music library
24|
25|The library is a static `public/music/manifest.json`, version 2, fetched
26|by the client from `/music/manifest.json`. A static file needs no route,
27|ships from the CDN, and swaps by replacing files only. Tracks may be
28|several minutes long and are not loops unless marked so.
29|
30|`MusicManifest = { version, tracks }`. `Track = { id, src, title,
31|emotion, vector, intensity, tempo, durationSec }` plus optional
32|`startSec` (default 0, where playback starts on first play and on each
33|loop), `loop` (default true), `source` (`generated`, `jamendo`, or
34|`recording`), `artist`, `composer`, `license`, `attribution`, and
35|`sourceUrl` (https only). `emotion` is the hand label: one of the 8
36|emotion ids in `core/types.ts`. The vector covers the 8 ids with finite
37|entries in 0..1. `core/music.ts` owns `parseManifest`, which rejects
38|unknown versions, missing fields, bad vectors, NaN entries, out-of-range
39|numbers, `startSec` outside its range, unknown `source` values, and any
40|`src` that is not a `/music/` path or `https` URL. The reader calls it on
41|every fetch, so a bad drop-in fails loudly in dev. Remote URLs need a
42|`media-src` addition in `next.config.ts`.
43|
44|## Similarity and config
45|
46|`Similarity = (scene, track, weights) => number`, where
47|`SceneSignal = { vector, intensity, tempo }`. The default is
48|`bhattacharyyaSimilarity`: both 8-emotion vectors renormalize to sum 1
49|(an all-zero vector gives an affinity of 0), `E` is the sum of
50|`sqrt(s_k * t_k)`, and the score is `weights.emotion * E` plus
51|`weights.intensity` and `weights.tempo` each for intensity and tempo
52|closeness. Scoring and ranking pass the resolved config weights in, so
53|a weights override changes the ranking. `cosineSimilarity` over
54|`buildFeatures` output stays as an exported alternative. One exported object,
55|`MUSIC_CONFIG`, holds `similarity`, `weights`, `switchMargin` (0.07),
56|`dwellSec` (20), `minTrackSec` (45), `hardCutMargin` (0.20),
57|`crossfadeSec` (3), and `hardCutCrossfadeSec` (1.5). Everything else
58|reads from it. Ranking ties go to the lower track id.
59|
60|## Selection scheduler
61|
62|`core/music-schedule.ts` is a pure state machine. The reader calls
63|`observeScene`, `tickScheduler`, `requestNext`, and `noteTrackEnded`
64|with explicit `nowSec` values, so all timing is testable without
65|timers. State holds the current track id and when it started, the active
66|scene id, the pending scene id and since when, and the skip override
67|with the scene it belongs to.
68|
69|A newly entered scene becomes pending and the dwell clock restarts, so
70|fast scrolling keeps only the newest scene. The first track ever plays
71|at once with no dwell. After the pending scene holds for `dwellSec` it
72|becomes active and the override clears. Then the best track switches in
73|only when it beats the current score by `switchMargin` and the current
74|track played `minTrackSec`, unless it wins by `hardCutMargin` (hard
75|cut, short fade). A second passes the active scene back through the
76|switch check, so a hold from `minTrackSec` releases on time, unless a
77|skip override stands: ticks return no change while it is set, and only
78|a new scene promotion clears it. A switch
79|reports its crossfade length: 3 s normally,
80|1.5 s for hard cuts. The skip choice holds until the next scene change;
81|after that, dwell and hysteresis apply with the override track as the
82|current track. A null scene means a failed analysis with no vector, so
83|it never triggers a switch. A non-looping track that ends fades into
84|the best remaining track, excluding the one that ended, and clears the
85|skip override.
86|
87|## Change track
88|
89|`nextTrack` cycles tracks hand-labeled with the scene dominant emotion
90|(argmax of the renormalized scene vector, ties by emotion order), ranked
91|by score with ties by lower id, wrapping around and skipping the current
92|track. When the current track has another emotion, it starts at the top
93|candidate. With no other same-emotion track it falls back to the best
94|track overall that is not current. A null scene cycles all tracks in id
95|order. One track or none gives null, and the UI disables the button.
96|
97|## Player
98|
99|`app/player.tsx` takes the track, the fade length for the latest switch,
100|the scene title, a skip flag, and callbacks. It owns two `audio`
101|elements, play state, volume, and the equal-power crossfade
102|(cos/sin gains over the fade time, driven by `requestAnimationFrame`).
103|It never uses the `loop` attribute. Volume lives in a ref, so the slider
104|never re-runs the track effect or touches `src`. A new track request
105|mid-fade cancels the pending fade and fades from the audible element to
106|the newest track. On load each track seeks to `startSec` once metadata
107|is available. Long tracks with `loop` true crossfade into the other
108|element playing the same track from `startSec` when `currentTime`
109|reaches `duration - fade`, where `fade` is the latest scheduler fade
110|length, or the config `crossfadeSec` when none was reported yet. When
111|`loop` is false the player reports the end and the scheduler picks the
112|next-best track excluding the ended one. Pause stops both elements and
113|freezes the fade in place; play resumes the audible elements from the
114|frozen point. Audio starts once, on the first press, with fade 0.
115|Audio starts only after the user presses play. Reduced motion is read in
116|state with a change listener and affects visuals only, never the fade.
117|
118|The bar shows Play/Pause, Volume, a Change track button (disabled when
119|Next has nothing to offer), the track title with its emotion label, and
120|attribution when present: composer or artist, license, and a source
121|link. On manifest failure the reader still renders and the bar shows a
122|short neutral note. UI motion stays under 200 ms. Controls are real
123|buttons and inputs with labels, visible focus, and keyboard use.
124|
125|## Image api
126|
127|`POST /api/images` (Node runtime, `maxDuration` 120). Request is a
128|discriminated union: `{ kind: "passage", bookId, textVersion, n }` names
129|the paragraph where the selection starts, `{ kind: "scene", bookId,
130|textVersion, sceneId }` names the scene. Validation is strict: known
131|book, matching `textVersion`, integer `n` inside the book, known
132|`sceneId`. Any other body is a 400 with a generic Spanish message.
133|The client sends ordinals and ids only, never text.
134|
135|Responses (typed in `core/types.ts`): `{ status: "ready", url, cached,
136|caption }` with a Vercel Blob URL, never bytes; `{ status: "pending" }`
137|when another request holds the lock, in which case the client reposts
138|every 3 s up to about 2 minutes; `{ status: "error", code, message }`
139|where code is `quota`, `budget`, `unavailable`, or `bad_request` with a
140|friendly Spanish message. Caption is the scene title for scenes and the
141|first words of the paragraph for passages, built server-side.
142|
143|The passage cache key is book plus start paragraph plus `textVersion`
144|plus `PROMPT_VERSION` (`v1`); the scene key is book plus scene id plus
145|the same versions. Both map to a deterministic Blob path
146|(`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). An Upstash Redis
147|index maps key to Blob URL, so hits are one GET; on an index miss the
148|server checks the Blob path before generating and backfills the index.
149|A Redis lock per key returns `pending` to concurrent requests. Quota is
150|5 new images per person per day by hashed IP and signed cookie,
151|whichever runs out first; a shared spend counter in integer
152|micro-dollars sits under `SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 10). Failures refund
153|quota and budget and release the lock.
154|
155|## Chat api
156|
157|Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN,
158|spoilerMode, messages }` carries the chat history and the reader
159|position. The response is streamed text. The server builds context from
160|the book text up to `positionN`, or the whole book when `spoilerMode` is
161|on, with the book prefix first and the question last so readers share
162|the prompt cache. The system prompt answers only from that text and
163|refuses the rest. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
164|
165|## Quotas and budget
166|
167|Server only. Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars: reserve with
168|Redis `INCRBY` before each model call, refund with `DECRBY` after, one
169|reserve per call including retries. The server clamps every model tool
170|argument. Clients never see keys or raw errors. Generic messages go to
171|the client, details stay in server logs.
